about: The epistola of the formulary “Saint Matthew, Apostle and Evangelist” in the 1962 Roman Missal.

seg.tr: The likeness of the countenance of the four living creatures: the face of a man and the face of a lion on the right side of the four of them, but the face of an ox on the left side of the four of them, and the face of an eagle above the four of them. Their faces and their wings were stretched out above; two wings of each were joined together, and two covered their bodies; and each of them walked before its own face. Wherever the impulse of the spirit was, there they went, and they did not turn back when they walked. And as for the likeness of the living creatures, their appearance was like that of burning coals of fire, and like the appearance of lamps. This was the vision running here and there in the midst of the living creatures: the brightness of fire, and lightning going forth from the fire. And the living creatures went and returned, in the likeness of flashing lightning.
